'''Syed Mujahid Kamran''' (born 23 January 1951) is a Pakistani [[theoretical physicist]] and a former [[vice-chancellor (education)|vice-chancellor]] of the [[University of the Punjab]] in [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]].

He is a professor of [[physics]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Mujahid Kamran|publisher=University of the Punjab website|url=http://www.pu.edu.pk/faculty/pub/55002_pub.asp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110209171812/http://pu.edu.pk/faculty/pub/55002_pub.asp|archive-date=2011-02-09|access-date=28 November 2021}}</ref> and previously served as the chairman of the Physics Department at the [[University of the Punjab]]<ref name="dailytimes"/> (1995–2001) and (January 2007&nbsp;– January 2008). From 2004 to 2007, he served as the dean of the Faculty of Sciences at the same institution.<ref name="dailytimes"/> In January 2008, he was appointed [[vice-chancellor (education)|vice-chancellor]] of the Punjab University by the [[Governor of Punjab, Pakistan|governor of Punjab]], [[Khalid Maqbool]].<ref name="dailytimes">{{Cite news|last=Lodhi|first=Adnan|title=Prof Dr. Mujahid Kamran appointed new PU VC|newspaper=Daily Times (newspaper)|date=4 January 2008|access-date=28 November 2021|url=http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/default.asp?page=2008\01\04\story_4-1-2008_pg7_35|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080109024026/http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/default.asp?page=2008%5C01%5C04%5Cstory_4-1-2008_pg7_35|archive-date=9 January 2008|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Kamran joined the [[University of the Punjab]] as a lecturer in 1972 and became an assistant professor in 1982, associate professor in 1986, and professor in 1988.<ref name="dailytimes"/> He is a former [[Fulbright Fellow]]<ref name="dailytimes"/> at the [[University of Georgia]] from 1988–89.

==Early life and education==
Kamran was born on 23 January 1951, in [[Gujrat city|Gujrat]], Pakistan.<ref name="cv"/> In his early youth, he moved to [[Rawalpindi]], where his father, Syed Shabbir Hussain, took a position as a [[political journalism|political correspondent]] for the ''[[Pakistan Times]]''. From 1955 to 1969 he studied at the educational institutions of Rawalpindi. In 1965, Kamran did his [[matriculation]] from [[Sir Syed Ahmad Khan|Sir Syed High School]],<ref name="dailytimes"/> standing first in the class.<ref name="cv"/> Kamran later did his F.Sc. in 1967 and BSc in 1969 from [[Gordon College (Pakistan)|Gordon College]], Rawalpindi.<ref name="dailytimes"/><ref name="cv">{{Cite web | last = Kamran | first = Mujahid | title = Curriculum vitae (CV) | date = 7 July 2015|access-date=28 November 2021|url = http://www.mujahidkamran.com/uploads/MK_CV_2015.pdf |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151105205318/http://www.mujahidkamran.com/uploads/MK_CV_2015.pdf | archive-date = 2015-11-05}}</ref>

He attended the [[University of the Punjab]] and earned an MSc in physics in 1971,<ref name="dailytimes"/> specialising in theoretical particle physics. He won merit scholarships during the periods 1965–1967, 1967–1969, 1969–1971.<ref name="dailytimes"/> He was awarded a doctoral scholarship by the [[Government of Pakistan]] under the Central Overseas Training Scholarship Scheme and travelled to Great Britain to attend the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1975. There, he received a PhD in [[theoretical physics]] in 1979.<ref name="dailytimes"/><ref name="cv"/><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Muḥammad|first=Aḥmad, 'Abd El-Gādir|date=1993|title=Dual absortive model and elastic hadronic scattering at high energies and small momentum transfers|language=en|hdl=1842/15135}}</ref> His doctoral thesis was titled "The Dual Absorptive Model and Elastic Hadronic Scattering at High Energies and Small Momentum Transfers" and was supervised by Dr. L.L.J. Vick.<ref name="cv"/>

==Academic career==
After completing his PhD, Kamran returned to Pakistan in 1979, and joined his alma mater as lecturer in physics. He has been teaching postgraduate (MSc and M.Phil) and undergraduate (BSc Hons) classes at Punjab University (PU). He has also taught PhD, MSc and BSc courses at [[King Saud University]] (KSU) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where he was an associate professor from 2001 to 2004. KSU has an American system with a BSc awarded after 16 years, and MSc after 18 years of education. Courses he taught at PhD and MSc level at KSU were: Physics of Elementary Particles, [[Quantum Field Theory]] I and II, [[Gauge Theory|Gauge Theories]], Mathematical Physics, and Quantum Mechanics II. He also taught [[Quantum Mechanics]] at the BSc final year level.

After becoming the chairman of the Physics Department in May 1995,<ref name="dailytimes"/> he initiated a program of grooming talented students (through extra lectures and coaching) so that they could win foreign scholarships. Owing to his efforts, PU physics students have won about 40 fellowships (worth about 3 million dollars) since 1999. This program was initiated well before GOP/HEC launched its manpower training programs. Not a single penny of the GOP/HEC has been spent in this regard as these scholarships are funded by Western institutions. Prof. T. Bolton of [[Kansas State University|KSU]] referred to him as "a goldmine of graduate students". He was conferred with the [[Pride of Performance]] award in 1998.<ref>{{cite web
 |author      = ICTP

 |archive-date = 18 May 2012
 |df          = dmy-all
}}</ref>

 |archive-date = 8 March 2012
 |df          = dmy-all
}}</ref> He also published a brief book on the life of Albert Einstein, titled ''Einstein and Germany''.<ref>{{cite news| title =A Troubled Relationship| newspaper =Dawn (newspaper)|date =18 July 2010|url =https://www.dawn.com/news/827655/a-troubled-relationship|access-date =28 November 2021| url-status =live|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160304063331/http://www.dawn.com/news/827655/a-troubled-relationship| archive-date=4 March 2016| df =dmy-all}}</ref>

==9/11 claims==
In 2013, Kamran published a book entitled ''9/11 and the New World Order''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ULOvngEACAAJ|title=9/11 and the New World Order|author=Mujahid Kamran, Syed Ghulam Sarwar|publisher=University of the Punjab|date=2013|access-date=29 November 2021|isbn=978-9699325137|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629134525/https://books.google.com/books?id=ULOvngEACAAJ|archive-date=29 June 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In this book, he has tried to substantiate some of the popular [[9/11 conspiracy theories]]. In an article on 24 September 2012, he wrote that "currently 95% of the [[US media]] is owned by only six corporations, whose top echelons are dominated by [[Zionists]] allied with the banking cabal. With the US military and intelligence apparatus in their control, with their ownership of the media, and with their control of academia, it is easy for them to direct assassinations and [[false flag]] operations, such as the murder of [[JFK]] and [[9/11]]."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mujahidkamran.com/articles.php?id=42 |title=9/11 – An Analysis|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222101246/http://www.mujahidkamran.com/articles.php?id=42 |archive-date=22 February 2016|access-date=29 November 2021}}</ref>

On 11 September 2013, while taking part in a talk show on the Pakistani 24-hour news channel Din News, he supported the 9/11 conspiracy theories.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://pu.edu.pk/home/section/allpress/2899 | title=American people the finest group of mankind: PU VC - University of the Punjab - Press Release }}</ref><ref name=Tribune>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/603091/911-and-the-new-world-order-mujahid-kamran-reveals-plot-to-take-over-the-world/|title = 9/11 and the New World Order: Mujahid Kamran reveals plot to take over the world|date = 11 September 2013|access-date=29 November 2021|newspaper=The Express Tribune (newspaper)}}</ref> He blamed the international bankers for all the ills in the world. He also criticised the US think tanks such as the [[Council on Foreign Relations]] for pushing the US into wars.<ref name=Tribune/>

==Personal life==
As a young student, Kamran was a keen field hockey player and a science debater. He was a member of the Gordon College hockey team (1967–1969)<ref name="cv"/> as well as the Punjab University hockey team (1969–1971). He was captain of the PU hockey team between 1970 and 1971.<ref name="cv"/> He was a member of the Gordon College House of Commons Debating Club from 1965 to 1969<ref name="cv"/> and was president of the Punjab University Physics Association from 1970 to 1971.

Kamran is the son of veteran journalist, scholar and former bureau chief of The Pakistan Times, Islamabad, Syed Shabbir Hussain. He has three brothers and two sisters.

* National Book Foundation Award (1997)<ref name="dailytimes"/>
